subject: Europe region availability & security questionnaire kickoff
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: jonathan.green@acmehealth.com, procurement@acmehealth.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Europe region availability & compliance next steps

Hi Jonathan / Acme procurement team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciate the clear rundown of your regulatory constraints (HIPAA for clinical notes ingestion + GDPR residency requirements for EEA patient records). I wanted to capture the concrete follow-ups and owners so we can move quickly on your procurement timeline.

Summary of what we covered:
- Region availability: Redwood currently has EU-region inference capacity (Frankfurt and Amsterdam). We can route production traffic to the EU-only tenancy for data residency.
- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II (reported 2026 Q4). We can provide the summary and a redacted report under an NDA.
- HIPAA: We support HIPAA customers via our Private deployment option + BAAs; hosted API is available in dedicated instances with contractual protections.
- Export controls: There are a few export-control considerations (OFAC sanctions screening + potential ITAR implications for model weights). For your use case (processing EEA patient data into inference only), primary items are cross-border transfer controls and vendor-attestation.

Immediate next steps / owners:
1) Vendor Security Questionnaire (VSA): procurement to complete our standard spreadsheet. I attached a pre-filled workbook with answers to common SOC 2 and GDPR questions (see attachment). Owner: Acme procurement; Redwood contact: Marissa Cole.
2) SOC 2 artifact request: Jonathan — if you can send the NDA link, Rishi will share a redacted SOC 2 Type II. Owner: Rishi.
3) Residency confirmation: Dev will capture infra routing and produce a short note on data flow and whether any cross-border caching may occur. Owner: Dev Patel.
4) Export control check: I will list the limited set of policies and ask legal to confirm whether any special exports approvals are necessary for your EEA dataset. Owner: Hannah.

Timing: you mentioned procurement aims to have vendor security homework completed by the end of next week. If that still holds, we will prioritize the SOC 2 share and the residency note by Tue 23 Mar.

Attachments:
- vendor_security_questionnaire_acme.xlsx (pre-filled answers)
- redwood_soc2_summary_2026.pdf (one-page summary)

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up with procurement if helpful.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai

From: Jonathan Green <jonathan.green@acmehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:14:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Europe region availability & compliance next steps

Hannah — thanks for the clear recap. Two quick clarifications from our end: 

1) The BAA is required for any PHI processing. Can you confirm whether the Private deployment is the only route for a BAA, or can Dedicated pools with contractual commitments satisfy HIPAA?
2) For SOC 2, we'll need the Type II report (redacted is fine) before legal signs off. We'll share the NDA link by EOD today.

Procurement timeline remains end of next week for VSA completion. I put Dev and Rishi in copy so they can coordinate directly.

— Jonathan
Director of IT Security, Acme Health
jonathan.green@acmehealth.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Jonathan Green <jonathan.green@acmehealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 12:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Europe region availability & compliance next steps

Jonathan — appreciate the prompt. Short answers first: 

- BAA: We support BAAs. Hosted shared tenancy typically does not satisfy HIPAA controls due to multi-tenant logs and telemetry. However, Dedicated customer pools and Private deployments are common patterns to meet HIPAA requirements. We'll include the exact control mappings in the SOC 2 artifact pack.
- SOC 2 report: NDA received (thanks) — I'll share a redacted Type II PDF by EOD tomorrow.
- Data flow / residency: for Hosted Dedicated in EU, we can ensure ingress, inference, and logs remain in the EU region; there are one-time migration steps for KV-cache sharding to ensure no transient cross-region replication.

Notes for your legal team: 
- We perform OFAC sanctions screening at onboarding and on exported logs when required. For ITAR — unless your dataset contains controlled technical data, risk is low for typical EHR text. If you have flagged records that might be ITAR-related, flag them and we will route to legal for a more detailed export control assessment.

I will attach the redacted SOC 2 and a control-mapping spreadsheet for your info.

-rishi
Sr. Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

- Tab 2: Data residency — see cell B14 where we indicate EU-only tenant options and the steps to lock routing to EU regions.
- Tab 3: Export controls — we flagged OFAC / ITAR-related questions for your legal review; please mark any dataset concerns in column F and we'll triage.

Action items: 
1) Procurement: review Tab 1–3 and mark any follow-ups by Fri 26 Mar.
2) Dev (Redwood): create a 1‑page technical note on caching/replication for EU Dedicated (target Wed 24 Mar).
3) Rishi: share redacted SOC 2 Type II (target Tue 23 Mar).

Attachments: vendor_security_questionnaire_acme.xlsx

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
